name: Dali Old Town (Gucheng)
description: The historic core, ringed by old walls, with cobbled streets, Bai white-walled houses, teahouses, cafes, and craft shops. It is the center of the traveler and slow-living scene, atmospheric and lively but the most touristy part of Dali, especially along the busy main lanes.
pros: Best concentration of cafes and nomad hangouts
cons: Very touristy and commercialized in parts

name: Erhai Lakeshore Villages (Caicun, Shuanglang)
tagline: Lake views and slow village life
description: A string of Bai villages along Erhai lake, from nearby Caicun to the popular Shuanglang on the far shore. Known for guesthouses, lake-view cafes, cycling paths, and boat trips, these spots trade old-town bustle for water, sunsets, and a mellower, scenic rhythm.
bestFor: Nature lovers and longer slow-living stays
cons: Shuanglang can get busy with tourists

name: Cangshan Mountain Foothills
tagline: Above the town, into the mountains
description: The green slopes rising west of the old town toward the Cangshan range. Home to scattered guesthouses, retreats, and trailheads, this area offers cooler air, hiking, cable-car access, and sweeping views over Erhai lake, favored by those wanting quiet and nature over street life.
pros: Direct access to trails and cable cars
cons: Steeper and less convenient for daily errands

name: Xiaguan (New Dali)
tagline: The modern city and transport hub
description: The contemporary downtown about half an hour south of the old town, home to the high-speed rail station, long-distance buses, hospitals, and big shopping. It lacks the old-town charm but offers everyday convenience, cheaper local rents, and the practical infrastructure of a real working city.
cons: Away from the scenic old town and lake
